CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right upper arm pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
The patient is a 39-year-old female presenting with severe right upper arm pain that occurred 18 hours ago during a volleyball game. She reports spiking a volleyball when an opposing player kicked her legs from underneath her as she was jumping. She fell and landed on her right shoulder/arm. She rates her pain as 9/10. She has been taking ibuprofen every 6 hours with minimal relief. She has not applied ice. X-ray imaging reveals a proximal humerus fracture.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies numbness or tingling in the right arm. Patient reports swelling and redness over the right shoulder.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Gallstones.
Lumbar fusion approximately 6 years ago.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen every 6 hours.
Pepcid.

ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Plays volleyball.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right shoulder with visible swelling and erythema. Tenderness over right shoulder. Patient able to straighten elbow when shoulder is not moved. Normal pulses in right arm. Normal motor function. No numbness or tingling in right arm. Rest of body examination normal.

RESULTS
X-ray of right arm demonstrates proximal humerus fracture.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Proximal humerus fracture. Plan to immobilize with long arm cast and sling. Follow-up examination in 2 weeks to assess bone realignment; surgery may be considered if bones do not realign appropriately. Prescribed Lortab 5 mg, 1-2 tablets every 6 hours as needed for pain (20 tablets dispensed). Patient to be fitted with cast by technician prior to discharge.
